Everybody Blames the Wrong Worm 🪱 Evil Dead, Earthworm Jim and the Real "Groovy" Thief

short // Sep 30, 2026

Watch on TikTok

Everybody blames the wrong worm. 🪱

Every time somebody hears Earthworm Jim yell "Groovy!", the comments fill up with the same accusation: he stole it from Ash. But Jim has been taking the heat for somebody else. The real "Groovy" thief has been hiding in plain sight the whole time, wearing sunglasses. 🕶️

Where "Groovy" comes from

"Groovy" belongs to Ash Williams. Bruce Campbell's Ash says it in Evil Dead II (1987), right after he straps a chainsaw where his hand used to be. By Army of Darkness (1992), it was part of his whole act, right next to "Hail to the king, baby," "Shop smart. Shop S-Mart" and the boomstick.

So when people hear "Groovy" in a '90s game, they think of Ash first. Fair enough.

The accused: Earthworm Jim

Earthworm Jim hit the Sega Genesis and Super Nintendo in 1994: a regular earthworm in a super-powered space suit. He was created by Doug TenNapel, who also voiced Jim in the games. Jim's catchphrase is an excited "Groovy!", and he kept it in the cartoon, too.

Here's the thing, though. "Groovy" is old slang, way older than Ash. It comes out of jazz-era talk about being "in the groove," and by the '60s it was everywhere. A goofy, over-the-top cartoon worm shouting it after a win makes total sense without any Evil Dead connection.

And Jim only shares the one word. He doesn't copy Ash's attitude, his look or the rest of his lines, and I couldn't find any evidence that his "Groovy!" was lifted from Ash.

The real thief: Duke Nukem

Now look at Duke Nukem 3D (1996). Duke doesn't borrow one word. He borrows Ash's whole personality:

  • "Groovy!" That's Ash, Evil Dead II.
  • "Hail to the king, baby!" That's Ash in Army of Darkness, and it became Duke's signature line.
  • "Good, bad, I'm the guy with the gun." Ash again, Army of Darkness.

He didn't stop at Ash, either. "It's time to kick ass and chew bubble gum, and I'm all outta gum" comes straight from Roddy Piper in They Live. Even the Duke Nukem 3D box art mirrors Ash's pose on the Army of Darkness poster, and Bruce Campbell reportedly wasn't thrilled about any of it.

That's not a coincidence. That's the real thief, hiding in plain sight behind a pair of sunglasses.

Innocent worm or nah?

My verdict: innocent worm. Jim yelled a word that was already decades old. Duke walked off with Ash's lines, his swagger and his poster pose.

Ash should be looking at the guy in the shades, not the worm in the space suit.

Sources: Duke Nukem 3D quotes (Duke Nukem Wiki), Wikipedia: Earthworm Jim, Wikipedia: Army of Darkness, TV Tropes: Army of Darkness references

Quick answers

Who said "Groovy" first, Ash or Earthworm Jim? Ash said it in Evil Dead II in 1987, seven years before Earthworm Jim came out in 1994. The word itself is much older slang.

Did Earthworm Jim steal "Groovy" from Ash? There's no evidence of that. "Groovy!" is Jim's catchphrase, but the word was common slang for decades before either character existed.

Did Duke Nukem copy Ash from Evil Dead? Duke Nukem 3D (1996) uses several of Ash's lines, including "Groovy!" and "Hail to the king, baby!", and its box art mirrors Ash's pose on the Army of Darkness poster.

Who created Earthworm Jim? Doug TenNapel, who also voiced Jim in the original games.
